correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact Bernoulli-subset Bernstein coefficients c[e,h,k]/n with n-2 surviving edges. Independent program exhaustively checked every Prüfer word and threshold for n=2..5 (1,6,48,500 = 555 labeled-tree/threshold cases), finding coefficientwise dominating cuts. Independently matched all five exact six-vertex broom risk polynomials: Q03=p², Q34=p²(9-5p)/6, Q01=Q02=p²(9-4p)/6, Q45=p²(12-9p+2p²)/6; differences show strict switch exactly p=3/5. The exhaustive finite n<=5 result is genuinely exhaustive, and polynomial nonnegative-basis identity proves all real p in [0,1], not a grid extrapolation.

value.rationale: Sharp first-order cutoff for a natural tail-risk epidemic-interdiction objective; exact nonnegative Bernstein certificate and a genuine intervention-ranking switch motivate this finite classification. Not an empirical control policy.

final_claim: In independent-bond tree epidemics with uniform seed, for each fixed outbreak threshold all trees of 2..5 vertices admit a transmissibility-independent optimal one-edge cut; six is sharp with explicit size-three broom switching at p=3/5.
limitations: Homogeneous independent edge transmission, uniformly drawn seed, one preemptive cut, tree, threshold event; not general SIR with dependent transmissions.
Computer-exhaustive bound only for n<=5; continuum parameter follows polynomial identity.
